plan.title: Jab, Jab, Jab, Right Hook
plan.author: Gary Vaynerchuk
plan.confidence_note: I know the book's core framework, its platform-by-platform structure and its style of critiquing real brand posts well, but not every specific example in detail.
plan.one_liner: Give value again and again before you ask, and speak each platform's native language.
plan.summary: Gary Vaynerchuk argues that social media is a boxing match for attention. Jabs are the small, generous pieces of content that entertain, inform or delight your audience without asking for anything. The right hook is the moment you finally ask: buy, sign up, visit. Most brands throw right hooks nonstop and wonder why nobody responds. The book's second big argument is that context matters as much as content. Each platform has its own culture, format and etiquette, so a story must be shaped natively for Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest, Instagram, Tumblr and whatever comes next. Through annotated critiques of real brand posts, he shows what works and what flops. The takeaway is practical: give consistently, tell stories that fit the medium, make your ask clear and easy, and keep adapting as platforms change.
